# AI Insights

> AI Insights reads a person's local Claude Code and Codex history and turns it into one private HTML report: where their time and tokens go, what keeps going wrong, and specific changes to try. Everything runs on their machine; AI Insights makes no network calls and never calls a model API.

- Package: ai-insights on npm (Node.js 20 or newer)
- Source: https://github.com/hamedmp/ai-insights (MIT)
- Sample report, built from invented sessions: https://hamedmp.github.io/ai-insights/demo/report.html

## What it reads

- Claude Code: ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl (or under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR)
- Codex: ~/.codex/sessions and ~/.codex/archived_sessions (or under CODEX_HOME)
- Cursor, Pi and OpenCode can run the skills, but their own history is not read yet, and those installs are untested.

It keeps numbers (tokens, durations, tool calls, errors, lines changed) and the prompts the person typed, with secrets redacted. It does not store agent replies or tool output. It writes only to ~/.ai-insights/ (AI_INSIGHTS_HOME moves it; a ~/.hindsight/ folder from before the rename to AI Insights keeps being used).

## Install

Claude Code:

    /plugin marketplace add hamedmp/ai-insights
    /plugin install ai-insights@ai-insights

Codex:

    codex plugin marketplace add hamedmp/ai-insights
    codex plugin add ai-insights@ai-insights

Several harnesses at once: clone the repository and run scripts/install.sh (--dry-run shows what it would do).

Each install adds the MCP server (npx -y ai-insights mcp) and three skills: analyze-ai-usage (builds the report), ai-insights-coach (turns findings into edits the person approves), ai-insights-setup (checks the setup). Then, in a new session, the person asks their agent to "analyze my AI usage" (or runs /analyze-ai-usage).

Without an agent: `npx ai-insights` builds the numbers-only report; `npx ai-insights doctor` shows which history it found.

## How it works

1. Deterministic scan: sessions, activity, token usage, estimated cost at API list prices, and findings with evidence. No model involved.
2. The person's own agent reads short redacted excerpts, labels each sampled session from a fixed taxonomy (goal, outcome, friction, what went well), and writes a short narrative.
3. Both become one self-contained HTML report that loads nothing from the network.

Built by the Matrix OS team: https://matrix-os.com
